interactions.summary: Jiang ties a student's answer directly to Augustine's City of God, then affirms another student's view that heaven involves connection to God and release from ego and fear that bind people to the material world.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang response with two student answers

interactions.summary: A student imagines a highly personalized heaven populated by ancestors, martial-arts fantasy, Buddhist and Christian imagery, and luminous transformed bodies; Jiang summarizes the idea as an individualized heaven that becomes whatever one perceives it to be.

Jiang formally begins Paradise: Dante's pilgrim has reached heaven, Beatrice is now his guide, the heavens are arranged in nine spheres, and the workshop's first task is to understand Dante's unique cosmology and why he built it this way.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang lecture monologue leading into the text

claims.claim: Jiang treats the standard Christian image of heaven beside God singing in unison as recognizably Augustinian and explicitly links a student's answer to Augustine's City of God.
Ego and fear are described by Jiang as forces that bind human beings to the material world.
Jiang accepts the idea that heaven can be individualized, meaning that one's perception helps constitute what heaven becomes.
In Paradise, Dante is a pilgrim traveling through the universe toward God with Beatrice, his long-lost love, as guide.
claims.temporal_scope: Lecture framing of the poem on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: Dante's heaven is divided into nine spheres.
Jiang says Dante's conception of heaven is unique and that the workshop's first two days will focus on understanding that cosmology and the reasons for its construction.

signature_moments.moment: Heaven can be individualized: whatever you truly perceive it to be, it becomes.
signature_moments.source_phrase: whatever you perceive it is, it becomes
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This crystallizes Jiang's willingness to let imaginative participation shape the ontology of heaven rather than reduce it to doctrine alone.

signature_moments.moment: Dante's heaven is not generic afterlife scenery but a unique cosmos whose structure has to be interpreted.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Dante's perception or conception of the heavens is unique
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It names the governing project of the workshop: not merely reading lines but uncovering the logic of Dante's universe.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The Christian thinker Jiang invokes to identify the student's God-centered answer as Augustinian.
Dante's long-lost love and guide through Paradise in Jiang's setup of the poem.
Jiang's word for Dante's structured understanding of the heavens and the universe.

chronology_notes.note: By packet 3 of the 2026-06-15 opening session, Jiang has moved from crowd definitions of heaven into the formal interpretive program: two days devoted to Dante's cosmology in Paradise.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student's imaginative heaven mixes several images through noisy ASR; the semantic pass preserves Jiang's stable synthesis of the answer rather than over-normalizing every fantasy detail.
